'''Araga''' is a [[rare mob]] [[mountain lion]] found in the [[Hillsbrad Foothills]]. She used to have a unique appearance, with a slight mane and a striped tail.  

==Taming Araga==
Considering her entirely unique appearance - she is the only cat with this skin - Araga is quite a prize for those hunters who love having special pets. However, Araga is one of the rarest cats in the game, if not the rarest, and as a result, probably the most difficult to find and tame. It can most likely be found around the [[Headland]], [[Corrahn's Dagger]] and [[Gavin's Naze]], where other unnamed mountain lions spawn.

Many hunters lament camping under [[Humar the Pridelord|Humar]]'s tree waiting for him to respawn, but in fact, he's a cakewalk compared to Araga. Humar's respawn timer is 6–8 hours, while Araga's is 24–36 hours. Humar spawns in the exact same spot every time and does not move around, while Araga can spawn ANYWHERE in Hillsbrad Foothills where mountain lions are capable of spawning, and she wanders. Humar's tree is remote and most players not specifically looking for Humar will never go there... while Araga's most likely spawn locations are in high-traffic questing and traveling areas.

If you go to the green cliffs in southern Alterac and see her, consider yourself lucky, as there are a number of factors working against the chance of just happening across her. The chances of a player coming across Araga on their way to [[Dalaran]] (for example), noticing her rare spawn status, killing her for the heck of it, and leaving the area as if they were never there, is very high. Something like that can happen the moment Araga is spawned. For a hunter looking to tame Araga, there is nothing you can really do except camp the site as much as possible and don't give up.

The easiest way to get this pet, and many others, is to wait until there is a server restart, and wait for her around the time she would respawn - in Araga's case, 24–36 hours after the restart.

==Loot==
Drops a randomly-enchanted [[uncommon]] item in the level range of 23 to 26.

==Biography==
[[File:Archmage Ansirem Runeweaver.jpg|thumb|Archmage Ansirem Runeweaver.]]
===Family and personal life===
When Ansirem was a student, he was not the top of his class. He created an enchanted gem to aid him in casting spells, but it only worked half the time. He intended to use it to help him cheat during his exams, but he failed them anyway. After learning that cheaters never prosper, he learned his magecraft the hard way.<ref name="QfP">''[[Quest for Pandaria]]'', part 2</ref>

Ansirem has a daughter named [[Catelyn the Blade|Catelyn]]. Rejecting the "boring life" of a mage, she decided to become a pirate and joined the [[Blackwater Raiders]]. Ansirem still cares for his daughter and has a few "friends" he keeps plied with gold in Booty Bay who keep him updated when things happen there.<ref name="QfP"/>

By the time of the [[Third War]], Ansirem was a member of the [[Council of Six]]. Moments after the death of [[Antonidas]], Ansirem was among the mages who fought outside [[Dalaran]] against [[Arthas Menethil]] and the [[Scourge]] when [[Kel'Thuzad]] was summoning [[Archimonde]].<ref>''[[Warcraft III: Reforged]]'': [[Under the Burning Sky (WC3 Undead)]]</ref>

[[Grand Magister Rommath]] still holds Ansirem (and [[Archmage Modera|Modera]]) in contempt for doing nothing when Grand Marshal [[Othmar Garithos|Garithos]] locked Prince [[Kael'thas Sunstrider|Kael'thas]] and his followers away in the [[Dungeons of Dalaran]].<ref>[[In the Shadow of the Sun]]</ref>

===World of Warcraft===
{{wow-section}}
Archmage Ansirem Runeweaver was a [[human]] [[quest giver]] located at [[Dalaran Crater]] in the [[Alterac Mountains]]. At some point, he at least worked with [[Baron Revilgaz]].<ref>[[Magical Analysis]]</ref> He once visited [[Stranglethorn]] and found a troll relic, a [[Catelyn's Blade|blade]], and later gave it to Catelyn who ran with it off.

===Cataclysm era===
{{novel-section}}
Ansirem Runeweaver remained at the site of the crater left behind by Dalaran's literally earth-shaking exit until the [[Cataclysm (event)|Cataclysm]] of the world. Despite his disappearance, he still served the Kirin Tor and was, in fact, a member of [[The Six]].<ref name="ToW">[[Jaina Proudmoore: Tides of War]]</ref>

Ansirem, [[Modera]], and a few other magi arrived near [[Booty Bay]] to save his daughter Catelyn when she and her crew were under attack from the [[Bloodsail Buccaneers]]. He gave her his cheating gem (having to admit where it came from, as the other magi knew about it) to pay off a debt to the [[Steamwheedle Cartel]], although he advised her to leave out the part of its unreliability when she sells it.<ref name="QfP"/>

Ansirem was present during the meetings of the [[Council of Six]] and [[Jaina Proudmoore]] who was asking for help in defending [[Theramore]] and attacking [[Orgrimmar]].<ref name="ToW"/>

===Legion===
{{Legion-section}}
{{Stub/Lore-section|info from the last quests}}
[[File:Archmage Ansirem Runeweaver Legion.jpg|thumb|Archmage Ansirem Runeweaver.]]
When [[Khadgar]] called for a vote to have the Horde return to Dalaran, Ansirem was the only member of the [[Council of Six]] besides Jaina who voted no. They were outvoted and Jaina left, leaving Khadgar to take over.<ref>[[Calling of the Council]]</ref>

[[Aethas Sunreaver]] sought to return to Dalaran after being expelled in the [[Purge of Dalaran]], and used the retrieval of [[Felo'melorn]] to help convince the council. Khadgar had the [[Council of Six]] take a vote. While Ansirem expressed doubt that Aethas wouldn't just betray them again, [[Karlain]] brought up that if Aethas had any ulterior motives he would have simply given Felo'melorn to one of his [[Sunreavers]]. Convinced by Karlain's words, Ansirem changed his vote to accepting Aethas back into the [[Kirin Tor]], although not as a member of the [[Council of Six|Six]].<ref>[[The Frozen Flame]]</ref>

===Dragonflight===
{{Df-section}}
As Modera was the only member of the [[Council of Six]] to hear the [[Radiant Song]], Ansirem questioned her on how it felt. He was subsequently fascinated to be told that "It was warm. Comforting. Like coming home."<ref>[[The Harbinger]]</ref>

===The War Within===
{{Tww-section}}
Ansirem agreed with moving Dalaran to [[Khaz Algar]] and was present for Khadgar's announcement in the [[Portrait Room]].<ref>[[A Mysterious Warning]]</ref>

==Forever==
{{forever-section}}
Ansirem was contacted by [[Elaadrin Evengale]], the [[skyborne]] leader of a group called the [[High Order]] who lived in [[Skywall]], the [[elemental plane]] of air. Their home island was collapsing, and they needed help, and through this contact with Ansirem, Elaadrin was able to ally his people with the [[Kirin Tor]] and [[Alliance]]. Ansirem and several Kirin Tor forces traveled to Skywall to help the skyborne fight [[Rohash]].<ref>[[Confront Lorthuna]]</ref>

In ''[[Forever]]'''s timeline, Dalaran removed its shield early, while the city was still under reconstruction. Ansirem can be found in the [[Violet Citadel]].

==In the RPG==
{{RPG-section}}
Ansirem Runeweaver was at the time of ''[[Lands of Conflict]]'' a leading member of the [[Kirin Tor]], and was the ruler of Dalaran.<ref>''[[Lands of Conflict]]'', pg. 90</ref> He lead a conclave of fellow wizards in their vigil of the (former) dome. He constantly moved about the dome’s periphery. He was a nice enough person, but said very little of what went on beneath the dome.<ref>''[[Lands of Conflict]]'', pg. 90 - 91</ref> Dressed in an elaborate violet robe, the bearded man stood with his eyes closed and his brow furrowed in concentration. He was quite tall, and, although he appeared fairly old, he stood perfectly still — reflecting a great deal of physical discipline. The man carried no obvious weaponry, but his arms were crossed in his robes, concealing both hands.

Ansirem Runeweaver was no stranger to combat, having helped defend the magical city of Dalaran for the better part of four decades. He was confident, but not cocky, and always seemed to know where best to strike for maximum effect. Upon engaging in combat, Ansirem’s first action was usually to summon additional help, immediately following with a series of offensive blasts directed at enemy spellcasters. He targeted arcane spellcasters first, then any healers or archers. If Ansirem appeared to be winning after the first few exchanges of a combat, he pressed the advantage with area-effect spells such as rain of fire or shockwave. If he thought he is losing, however, Ansirem would not hesitate to cast teleport and beat a hasty retreat back to his private sanctum in Dalaran.<ref>''[[Lands of Conflict]]'', pg. 92</ref>

==Authorship==

*The series [[The Schools of Arcane Magic]], [[Portals are NOT Garbage Bins!]] and [[The Fate of Apprentice Argoly]] in which he notes the death of one of his (now former) apprentices that fell from the edge of Dalaran while on a simple gathering errand for him, due to impairment from chewing [[Felweed]].
*He most likely is also the author of [[Legends of the Gurubashi, Volume 3]].

'''Deer''' are hoofed, plant-eating mammals, known for their slender legs, keen senses, and bony antlers that grow and drop off every year. They are found all over [[Azeroth]]. Male deer are called '''stags''', females are called '''does''', and younglings are called '''fawns'''. Despite being herbivores, stags are tough, fast, and territorial and can provide a challenge for any [[hunter]].<ref>[[Stag Mastery]]</ref> Cooked [[Stag Meat|deer meat]] is called [[Lean Venison|venison]].

==Types==
[[File:Riverland Doe.jpg|thumb|upright|A [[Riverland Doe]], a female deer in [[Stormsong Valley]] (''Legion'' model).]]
Deer come in several natural varieties, notably:
*{{RaceIcon|Reindeer}} [[Caribou]] are large deer native exclusively to the [[Borean Tundra]] in [[Northrend]].
*{{RaceIcon|Stag}} [[Elk]] are large deer distinguished by their prominent antlers and are found both in [[Azeroth]] and [[Bonich]].
*{{RaceIcon|Moose}} [[Moose]] are particularly large, antlered deer found in [[Highmountain]] on the [[Broken Isles]] and [[Stormsong Valley]] in [[Kul Tiras]].
*{{RaceIcon|Elk}} [[Reindeer]] are a variety of deer associated with the [[Feast of Winter Veil]].

Magical deer varieties include:
*{{RaceIcon|Dreamstag}} [[Dreamstag]]s are a type of deer found in the [[Emerald Dream]].
*{{RaceIcon|Runestag}} [[Runestag]]s are a type of deer native to [[Ardenweald]].
*{{RaceIcon|Thornbuck}} [[Thornbuck]]s are [[thornborn]] deer found in [[Drustvar]].
*{{RaceIcon|Cervid}} [[Cervid]]s are [[protoform]] deer found in [[Zereth Mortis]].

==In the RPG==
{{RPG-section}}
There are a wide variety of deer, some of which have horns year-round. Deer are typically medium-sized animals and faster than [[elk]]. Some varieties, such as impala, live in tropical regions, while mountain deer may have the ability to spring, allowing them to traverse rocky terrain at three-fourths their normal speed. From mountain deer to mighty northern alpine [[moose]], they are the primary prey of wolves and other predators. Humans typically hunt the smaller deer, while orcs prefer the challenge of an elk or moose.<ref>''[[Manual of Monsters]]'', pg. 164</ref>

Stags are common in forested areas throughout [[Azeroth]]. Though they generally avoid conflict, their mighty antlers and ferocity can make them difficult prey, and they may become aggressive when startled or gathered in larger groups. They are particularly aggressive during mating season in the fall, and only at this time are they commonly found with females.<ref>''[[Monster Guide Web Supplement]]'', pg. 22</ref>

Aliden has not been seen since the [[Cataclysm (event)|Cataclysm]], presumably having been killed by [[Lord Aliden Perenolde (quest)|Horde adventurers]]. ==Biography== ===Beyond the Dark Portal=== {{Novel-section}} Aliden was [[Aiden Perenolde|King Aiden Perenolde]]'s eldest son, and as such the crown prince of [[Alterac (kingdom)|Alterac]]. According to [[Terenas Menethil II]] of [[Lordaeron (kingdom)|Lordaeron]] (who disliked both father and son), Aliden was pampered as a youth, never knowing hardship or danger. As far as the [[Alliance of Lordaeron|Alliance]] was aware, there is no evidence that Aliden knew of his father's treacherous collaboration with the [[Old Horde|Horde]] during the [[Second War]]. Aliden spent the two years after the Second War trying to overcome the stigma that his father's betrayal had cast upon the [[Perenolde family]]. The prince's name came up in discussions among the Alliance's leaders on what to do with Alterac after the Second War. [[Thoras Trollbane]] was of the opinion that Aliden was "cut from the same cloth" as his father. Terenas Menethil believed him to be an unfitting leader with no real experience, but conceded that they had no right to deny him the throne should his father abdicate since he was the legal heir. Shortly before the [[Invasion of Draenor]], [[Horde of Draenor|Horde]] forces led by [[Teron Gorefiend]] and his ally [[Deathwing]] came to [[Ruins of Alterac|Alterac City]] to demand the [[Book of Medivh]], which Aiden had stolen. Aiden gave them the book in exchange for the Horde destroying the Alliance garrison occupying Alterac. Aliden witnessed part of the conversation and was able to recognize the Horde's [[death knight (Old Horde)|death knights]], indicating some sort of military familiarity. When he realized what his father had done, Aliden confronted him and punched him in the face, saying that he had ruined Aliden's efforts to try to clear the family name. Prince Aliden's fears seemingly proved right, as there is no mention of anyone supporting his claim to the throne during the later [[Alterac crisis]].''[[Day of the Dragon]]'', chapter 1, 2, 6 Aliden later joined the [[Durnholde military]]. He rose through its ranks alongside his friend, [[Captain Skarloc]],[[Captain Skarloc#Adventure Guide]] under the mentorship of [[Aedelas Blackmoore]] (who was coincidentally also the son of a [[Aedelyn Blackmoore|notorious traitor]]).''[[Arthas: Rise of the Lich King]]'', chapter 4 At some point prior to the [[Third War]], Aliden left Blackmoore's service to take up operations in the [[Alterac Mountains]]. ===World of Warcraft=== {{wow-section}} Aliden became the leader of the [[Syndicate]]. He styled himself lord of the Alterac Mountains and planned to [[Slavery|enslave]] the [[orc]]s that stood against him, just as his father and his mentor Blackmoore had planned. He lived in the manor of [[Dandred's Fold]] alongside his mistress, [[Elysa]].[[Lord Aliden Perenolde (quest)]] Also, like Aedelas Blackmoore, Lord Aliden had close ties with an orc named [[Nagaz]] (a member of the [[Argus Wake]]), reminiscent of Blackmoore and his pet orc gladiator [[Thrall]]. Thrall sent an expedition to Alterac to investigate the Syndicate and to retrieve [[Taretha's Necklace|a necklace]] which had belonged to his childhood friend, [[Taretha Foxton]].[[The Rescue]] Coincidentally, the necklace was in Elysa's possession. The Syndicate captured and enslaved the expedition, and Aliden—accompanied by Elysa—personally spoke with their leader [[Gol'dir]] in [[Strahnbrad]]. Gol'dir recognized Elysa's necklace and later told Horde [[adventurer]]s of it when they came to rescue him. [[Krusk]], another member of the expedition, sent the adventurers to kill Aliden, to show the Syndicate that the orcs wouldn't submit to them, and at the same time get the necklace. The adventurers traveled to Dandred's Fold and killed Aliden. Elysa pleaded for her life, claiming that Aliden had had her against her will, and gave the adventurers the necklace, saying she wanted "no memory of him".[[Taretha's Gift]] ==Abilities== *{{Abilities|Power Word: Shield|id=11974|Wraps an ally in a shield that lasts up to 30sec., absorbing damage. You stupid, selfish bastard, you've ruined everything!" ==In the RPG== {{RPG-section}} '''Aliden Perenolde''' is the son of [[Aiden Perenolde]] and the heir to the throne of [[Alterac (kingdom)|Alterac]].''[[Dark Factions]]'', pg. 158 He is in his 40s; though his body is strong, his grey hair shows his age. His clothing and armor often feature the [[Perenolde family|Perenolde]] crest.''[[Dark Factions]]'', pg. 159 Aliden currently leads the [[Syndicate]], a bandit group that includes Alterac's [[Nobles of Alterac|fallen nobles]] who seek to reclaim their kingdom.''[[Alliance Player's Guide]]'', pg. 159 ===Biography=== Aliden Perenolde was told from an early age that he would succeed his father as lord of Alterac. He was just beginning to make a name for himself in court when the [[Alliance of Lordaeron|Alliance]] sacked their capital city for his father's misdeeds. [[Aiden Perenolde]] was ultimately imprisoned, and any other collaborators were stripped of their titles and property, then imprisoned or exiled. Aliden's status as heir apparent was forgotten yet, the young Lord Perenolde dreamed of reclaiming his ancestral lands. Years later, he got his chance. While his father was rotting in prison, Aliden attempted to assume command of the exiled Alteraci, and eventually, from these exiled the [[Syndicate]] would be born. ====Third War==== Aliden was not content to be a lowly highwayman. He had since grown into a man as charismatic and ambitious as his father. He realized he had to do something drastic to reclaim his ancestral lands. Thus, when the [[Burning Legion]] and the [[Scourge]] assaulted [[Lordaeron]], he did not repeat his father's mistake by allying himself with the enemy. With the [[Lordaeron (kingdom)|Lordaeron]] kingdom crippled in the aftermath of the [[Third War]], he knew this was the time to strike. He convinced (or browbeat) the other nobles that this was the time for the Syndicate to attack openly and reclaim what was rightfully theirs. Simply taking advantage of the [[Alliance of Lordaeron|Alliance]]'s distraction, Aliden and his forces moved on his lands in the [[Alterac Mountains]]. The harried and panicked citizens, the people the nobles once ruled, were frightened and confused and put up little ﬁght, more concerned with the hellish creatures that rampaged over the land. In the mind of Aliden Perenolde and his peers, it was the Alliance that betrayed them, and not the other way around. ====The Syndicate==== When Aliden came up with the idea to take advantage of the Alliance's crippled state and attack neighboring lands, the Syndicate came under his rule, grudgingly. Little organization seems to exist beyond that, although [[Lord Falconcrest]] (who does not trust Aliden) has taken command in the [[Arathi Highlands]]. The Syndicate suffers from pride and jealousy, each noble wishing to be in Perenolde's position. There is a lot of inﬁghting. Even though the Syndicate regained much of its lands and more, Perenolde will not be satisfied until he takes [[Alterac City]] from the [[Crushridge]] [[ogre]]s, thus he has offered a great bounty to anyone who can reclaim his ancestral lands for him, though it is dubious he would honor such a bargain. One of the smarter decisions Perenolde made for the Syndicate was to break up the bandit gangs that joined them among the noble families, giving the bandits new allegiances so the gangs could not stay together to work against the nobles. This trick worked perfectly, and most bandits went along with it for the greater reward. The noble households (gangs of criminals, really) hold only nominal loyalty to Perenolde or each other, and thus greater forces are rare. Lord Perenolde knows he is a target for the nobles who chafe under his rule (including his children) and protects himself accordingly.''[[Dark Factions]]'', pg. 185 ===RPG notes=== *In ''[[Lands of Conflict]]'', Aliden is not mentioned but a character named [[Beve Perenolde]] (daughter of Aiden Perenolde) seemingly takes his role. '''Sheep''' are woolly domesticated bovids. They are commonly found wandering in the pastoral areas of [[Elwynn Forest]], [[Loch Modan]], the [[Redridge Mountains]], and [[Hillsbrad Foothills]] and even a few in the [[Alterac Mountains]], [[Westfall]], [[Gilneas peninsula|Gilneas]], and [[Howling Fjord]]. During the [[Second War|Second]] and [[Third War]]s, they were commonly seen in [[Lordaeron]], but most sheep in that area have apparently died. [[Black Lamb|Black sheep]] can only be found in [[Elwynn Forest]].<ref>[[Black Lamb]]</ref>

Male sheep are called [[ram]]s, female sheep are called ewes, and young sheep are called lambs. [[Mechanical sheep]] are robots that look like sheep created by engineers. [[Argali]] are a type of sheep found on the [[Dragon Isles]]. [[Mosswool]] are sheep-like earth elementals found on the [[Isle of Dorn]]. [[Ramolith]]s are ram-like earth elementals.

{{RPG-section}}
Sheep are docile herbivores. Both black and white varieties exist, and they are prized for their [[wool]]. Some [[mage]]s are infamous for [[polymorph]]ing their opponents into sheep. Sheep flee rather than attack. Rumors of them exploding spontaneously are unsubstantiated.<ref>''[[Monster Guide Web Supplement]]'', pg. 18</ref>

*The spell [[Polymorph]] allows mages to transform their enemies into sheep temporarily.
*In ''[[Warcraft II]]'', if annoyed, sheep will say "Baa-ram-ewe" which is a reference to the sheep's password from {{wp|Babe (film)|Babe, the gallant pig}}.
*In ''[[Warcraft III]]'', if a flying unit was polymorphed in lands where sheep were common, they became flying sheep. Likewise, if a waterborne creature were polymorphed, the unit could become two types of aquatic sheep.

Even though her title was warden, Belamoore seemed to be taking more time studying than anything. She studied a number of renegade [[Forsaken]], especially their leader [[Kegan Darkmar]], whom she had a growing respect for. She was engaged in studying the mysterious [[Bloodstone Artifacts]] that the group of Forsaken carried with them. After what her journal described as a long time, she discovered that the pendant she was working on could drink blood (she discovered this by accidentally cutting herself) and that fire, water, thunder, and rock were mixed with the blood within the stone. Lordamere Internment Camp did not have the manpower or the space to allow her to continue her research, so she decided to send it by courier to Dalaran. The courier never reached Dalaran and the stone was lost with him. Warden Belamoore hoped that the artifact did not fall into the wrong hands.<ref>[[Belamoore's Research Journal]]</ref>

Belamoore may have been killed during [[Prison Break In]], as she was part of the group that was guarding [[Kegan Darkmar]].

==In the RPG==
{{RPG-section}}
Warden Belamoore is a stern [[wizard]]ess who oversees the [[Lordamere Internment Camp]]. She oversees the wizards who now use the camp to imprison [[Forsaken]]. She does not exactly hate [[undead]], but desires to study them under controlled conditions. It is believed that perhaps she will invent something that will help defeat the [[Scourge]].<ref>''[[Lands of Conflict]]'', pg. 87</ref>
